card.title: I Predicted This
card.instruction: Create opportunities to show that each impossible event confirms a theory you understood long before anyone asked.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My notes say something would rise. The floating dog confirms it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An early metaphor for domestic elevation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Inspiration doesn't restrict itself to office hours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The dog's floating. My old notebook predicted household things would rise.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It says bread. Help me get him down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bread was the first case. My theory always included pets. Try 'sit.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He sat on the ceiling. Now the cat's joining him.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Independent confirmation! Bring the notebook; you'll want the chapter on getting them down.

mechanism: A turns a floating dog and then cat into confirmation of an old household-elevation theory, keeping the notebook central to the response.
confusable: Unlike merely revising a prophecy's wording after contradiction, A must seize the next impossible event as confirmation of a claimed prior explanatory model.
comparison: The pet alternative claims independent confirmation after a failed sit instruction; the cupboard alternative gains a new recognition request from speaking furniture.
